title: repeat_fork_keepkey
description: Residual keepKey hole after PR #34 finding 1 (typed-unnest and JSON-bridge forEach paths only): a fork branch that is (or chains into) a `repeat` whose body itself forks never receives `keepKey`, so the repeat body's fork CTE omits its `keyCols` and the enclosing fork's `JOIN … USING (keyCols)` fails with `Binder Error: Column "_rid" does not exist on right side of join!`. Two cases: (1) the fork branch is directly a `repeat` with a forking body; (2) the fork branch chains through `forEach: item` into a `repeat` with a forking body. Distinct values throughout so the order-independent Set comparison cannot mask a spurious cross-join row.

tests.title: direct repeat branch with a forking body recombines per resource (US1)
tests.description: The root forks on a repeat:[item] branch (body forking on forEach:answer + forEach:item) and a sibling forEach:basedOn. The repeat visits q1, q2, c1, c2; only q1 and q2 have both an answer and a child, so the INNER body fork yields per-node rows (a1, c1) and (a2, c2). These recombine with the two basedOn rows on the resource key.

tests.title: fork branch chaining through forEach into a forking repeat recombines per iteration (US2)
tests.description: The root forks on a forEach:item branch whose scope chains into a repeat:[item] with a forking body, and a sibling forEach:basedOn. Within group g1 the repeat visits q1 and c1 (only q1 forks to a row); within g2, q2 and c2. The branch's key carries the forEach:item iteration ordinal, so g1's rows never pair with g2's descent - a cross-join regression would instead produce four rows.
